newsitem.title: FRANCE: French channels adopt voluntary violence warnings.
newsitem.headline: French channels adopt voluntary violence warnings.

text.p: Four French television channels have agreed to mark violent or sexually explicit programmes with on-screen symbols to help parents control what their children watch, the CSA state broadcasting agency said on Wednesday.
Beginning on November 18, the TF1, France 2, France 3 and M6 channels will display a coloured symbol in a corner of the screen for certain programmes, CSA officials announced at a news conference.
None of France's cable channels has agreed to the plan. Nor has satellite channel Canal Plus nor Franco-German public culture channel Arte.
Under the scheme, "responsibility is shared between the television channels on the one hand and parents on the other, who must protect their children," CSA head Herve Bourges told reporters.
Bourges has been pressuring stations to adopt voluntary restraints on television violence, saying he was opposed to mandatory state controls on programming.
